transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-21 14:00 PST — Duration: ~52m. Attendees: Redwood - Samantha, Diego, Liam. Customer - Maya, Oliver, Sophie, Ethan.

Summary: Quick renewal check-in focused on committed uplift, adding EU sovereign region, and scope for a small on-prem pilot to satisfy data residency + KMS needs. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted options, and next steps: SOW, security docs, benchmark plan.

[00:00] Samantha: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Maya: yep loud and clear, thanks Sam.
[00:07] Sophie: hi all, Sophie from procurement, quick note — we only have 30 minutes today for pricing review, but we'll stay.
[00:12] Samantha: great, we have about 50 minutes, we'll keep it to the important bits. diego and liam are here to cover benchmarks and the onboarding path.
[00:20] Diego: hi! quick wave. i'll talk latency profiles and the on-prem pilot. small caveat, my mic stutters a little, so sorry if i drop.
[00:28] Oliver: that's fine.

[00:35] Samantha: ok we left off last quarter around a 15% uplift ask and sovereignty in the EU. since then we've prepared a proposal for dedicated committed units plus a 3-month burst buffer. main question for you: does that still match your expectations?
[00:48] Maya: functionally yes. our customer traffic has increased faster than the forecast on the summarization microservice. we need predictable throughput for peak weekdays, and the EU residency is hard req from legal.
[00:58] Oliver: and latency — for EU production we need p95 under 320ms for short-conversation sequences. current hosted endpoints were around 400 on our tests.

[01:12] Diego: right, that's where dedicated pools plus an EU edge/private node help. we measured baseline on the r2-family GPUs and in many cases drop to ~260-300 p95 when using the optimized kernel path and quantized weights. caveat — longer sequences push that up. also note kv cache behaviors matter, we sometimes see warmup penalties, the K-V cash (auto-transcriber wrote K-V cash — laugh) warm cache gives big wins.
[01:38] Maya: warm cache sounds good, how long until warm? we have a lot of cold-starts for new sessions.
[01:44] Diego: it depends on traffic and batch windows; with continuous batching and prefix caching we typically see cache warm in ~5-15 minutes for stable workloads; for bursty traffic we recommend a small always-on small pool to keep prefixes seeded.

[01:58] Sophie: clarifying contracts — we want committed units to be monthly with the ability to burst for at least 3 months at a defined uplift price. can you put that into the SOW?
[02:06] Samantha: yes. we'll draft SOW with committed unit amounts, a 20% cushion and explicit burst pricing and notice windows.

[02:15] Ethan: security question — on the private on-prem we need HSM integration, customer-managed KMS, and full audit logs. are these available?
[02:23] Liam: yes, the Private deployment supports KMS integrations and HSM via our key-mgmt adapters; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. we'll attach the security pack.
[02:31] Ethan: any limitations around bring-your-own-HSM (BYOH)? we have FIPS 140-2 hardware.
[02:36] Diego: BYOH is supported but there are ops details; the onprem package includes connectors. we'll need to validate key rotation and network egress flows during the pilot.

[02:47] Maya: can you run a realistic throughput test that mirrors our production traffic? we care about multi-tenant contention when several models hit the cluster.
[02:54] Diego: yes, that's what we're proposing for the on-prem pilot — a 72h throughput stress run with your prompt set. ideally we run a 24h smoke first to tune batching and instance sizing, then 48h full ramp.
[03:06] Oliver: and the benchmarks — will those be single-node or geocluster? we want to see EU-only numbers.
[03:11] Diego: EU-only; we'll stage a dedicated EU private node for the test. we can also run a cross-region test to validate failover/policy routing.

[03:21] Maya: timeline — we need EU production by July. is that viable?
[03:25] Samantha: yes, with the pilot in April and a two-month activation/provisioning and remediation period we'd be on track.

[03:33] Sophie: procurement question — if we commit to annual payment, will you extend a discount tier?
[03:38] Samantha: standard is tiered discounts for 12-month commitments — we'll show the delta between monthly vs annual in the SOW; we can also add ramp credits for the pilot.

[03:46] Oliver: on failover — if EU capacity flaps, we want automatic fallback to a compatible model in a different region rather than errors. is there a policy for that?
[03:53] Diego: smart routing can be configured with fallback policies; we'd set a primary EU model and a lower-capacity compatible variant in US-West as fallback with per-route thresholds. there is a small latency penalty but it preserves availability.

[04:05] Maya: question on quality — when you fallback to a quantized variant what's the expected drop in output fidelity?
[04:10] Diego: typically negligible for summarization but can be measurable for instruction tuning sensitive tasks. we recommend A/B evals on your eval set; Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

[04:22] Sophie: procurement — do you support PO and invoice net-30?
[04:26] Samantha: yes, PO accepted; standard is net-30 for enterprise. payment method and billing entity we'll confirm in the SOW.

[04:34] Ethan: a quick follow-up on logs/data retention — we need to keep logs for 12 months in-country for audits. is that configurable?
[04:41] Liam: retention policies are configurable in Private; for Hosted we have options but for in-country retention we strongly recommend Private/EU on-prem. we'll include retention options and data flow diagrams.

[04:52] Maya: are there any limitations on model versions? we want to pin a specific open model revision during the rollout.
[04:58] Diego: yes, you can pin model versions and rollouts. we support canary deploys and A/B, and automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected.

[05:08] Sophie: ok from procurement side, next steps are SOW and security pack. will you include pricing scenarios for committed vs burst?
[05:14] Samantha: yes. Items we'll send: updated SOW with committed uplift and burst clause, security docs (SOC2/ISO + KMS/HSM notes), on-prem pilot runbook, and cost/latency proforma.

[05:23] Maya: good. for the pilot we'll provide a masked dataset and a small eval set — we need to agree on PII handling.
[05:29] Ethan: i'll send the list of data classifications and our key rotation policy.

[05:34] Diego: note on the benchmark runbook: please include the exact prompt set and concurrency profile; i'll run a dry run internally first to set expectations.

[05:41] Samantha: any blockers from legal or procurement?
[05:44] Sophie: no blockers, just timeline alignment. we'll need the final SOW by March 24th to make our internal quarter planning.

[05:51] Samantha: understood. final recap: SOW & pricing by 3/24; sec pack + architecture by 3/25; benchmark runbook by 3/28; pilot week of April 11th. action items in the doc.
[05:59] Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:02] Samantha: thanks! i'll follow up with the links.

References & shared links mentioned during call:
- Onboarding deck (Redwood): https://redwood.app/notes/ceramic-harbor-onboarding-deck

- Benchmark runbook template: https://redwood.app/runs/benchmark-runbook-template

Transcript notes: occasional minor transcription errors (e.g., K-V cache transcribed as K-V cash), speaker overlaps at 03:50-04:00.

End of transcript.
